question: How can an IL-6R extracellular-domain sequence guide a reproducible VHH design lesson?
observations: UniProt identifies P08887 as the reviewed human interleukin-6 receptor subunit alpha entry, also named IL6R and CD126.
The record annotates residues 20-365 as extracellular, residues 366-386 as transmembrane, and residues 387-468 as cytoplasmic.
The extracellular annotation provides receptor context only; this case contains no VHH sequence, binding pose, affinity estimate, or ranking.
interpretation: The reviewed receptor entry can anchor a reproducible discussion of target identity and extracellular-domain scope before any separately authorized antibody research.
limitations: The case does not retrieve or retain the full P08887 sequence as an input artifact.
No structural epitope, antibody interaction, or candidate performance is established.
Rosalind launcher readiness is documented separately and does not establish a scientific run.
